hub_subtitle: Business English para seguros, reuniões e entrevistas — e o desbloqueio da fala, do primeiro dia ao último

lesson.menu_title: How Was It? -- Was and Were, and the Debrief After the Visit
lesson.menu_desc: A aula em que a Paula para de responder “fine”. Na aula 16 ela aprendeu a prometer o futuro com will; hoje ela volta ao passado para aprender as duas palavrinhas que descrevem como as coisas eram: was e were. Não é o que aconteceu (isso foi a aula 14) nem o que não aconteceu (aula 15) — é como foi: a viagem was longa, a sala was lotada, as perguntas were difíceis. E vem junto o conserto de um erro que ela já está prestes a cometer: adjetivo não anda com didn't — é I wasn't tired, nunca I didn't tired. A cena é a primeira vistoria dela sozinha, numa fábrica em Campinas, e a call de segunda em que o Greg faz a pergunta mais simples e mais difícil do mundo corporativo: “How was it?” Seis palavras novas (difficult, quiet, crowded, tired, useful, surprised), o relatório de vistoria na tela, e a Sofia contando o que o gerente técnico do cliente falou dela por telefone. -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 17 -- How Was It?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Paula Morales | Lesson 17 -- How Was It? (Was / Were)
lesson.grammar_point: past of the verb to be -- was for I/he/she/it and were for you/we/they, negative wasn't and weren't, and questions Was it...? / Were they...? / How was...?; adjectives and states take was/were, never didn't

listenings.text: Hi, Paula. David here. Today your lesson is about two very small words, was and were, and I want to tell you why they matter more than they look. When I came back from my first site visit, my manager asked me one question. How was it? And I said, it was fine. That was all. Fine. Two days later he asked me again, and this time he said, no, tell me how it was. Was the room crowded? Were the questions difficult? Were you tired at the end? And I started to talk, and I talked for ten minutes. He was not testing my English, Paula. He was teaching me something, and it took me years to understand it. A report says what happened. But how was it says what it was like, and that is the part people remember. So when somebody asks you how the visit was, please do not say fine. Say the drive was long. Say the room was crowded. Say the manager was difficult at the start. Say you were tired, but it was useful. Five short sentences, and now your colleague was there with you. That is the whole lesson. See you soon.

Good morning, Paula. Sofia here. I read your report from the visit on Friday, and I want to say three things. First, the numbers were right. Twelve people, six hours, fourteen technical questions. Nobody in this team writes a report that clean, so thank you. Second, and this is the important one, I called the client on Monday. The technical manager said your questions were good. He said you were slow, and then he said something I really want you to hear. He said, she was slow because she was careful, and careful is exactly what we want in a large risk. Third. Do you remember, in January, when you told me you were not ready to go alone? You were wrong, and I am very happy you were wrong. On Friday morning you were worried. On Friday night you were the person who did it. Paula, in November you will be in Miami, and somebody there will ask you, how was your first visit alone? Please do not say it was fine. Tell them everything. It was long, it was crowded, it was difficult, and it was yours. See you Thursday.

items.situation: Greg asks: 'How was the visit?' Do not answer with one word. Give him three sentences.
tips: It was long. The room was crowded, and the questions were difficult.
It was a hard day, but it was useful.

items.situation: A colleague thinks the meeting room was empty. It wasn't -- twelve people were there. Correct her.
tips: No, it wasn't empty. It was crowded.
It wasn't empty at all. Twelve people were in the room.

items.situation: Somebody asks how the technical questions were. Say they were difficult, and say who asked them.
tips: They were difficult. The technical manager asked most of them.
The questions were very difficult, and they were all from the technical manager.

items.situation: Ask Greg about his own first site visit. Start the question with 'How'.
tips: How was your first site visit?
How was it, your first visit alone?

items.situation: Sofia asks if you were tired on Friday night. You were -- but say the day was useful too.
tips: Yes, I was. I was very tired, but the day was useful.
I was tired, but it wasn't a bad day. It was useful.

items.situation: A colleague says: 'The twelve people at the factory were all engineers.' Only six were. Correct him.
tips: No, they weren't all engineers. Six were engineers.
They weren't all engineers -- six were, and the others were from the finance team.

bank.label: Describing how it was / Dizer como foi
items: I was tired, but it was useful.
The office was quiet on Monday morning.

bank.label: Asking and answering / Perguntar e responder
items: Yes, it was. / No, it wasn't.
No, they weren't. Six were engineers.
